LESSON: MY CREATION

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: My Creation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on My Creation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is a family the family tree?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. name family members in the nuclear and extended 

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MY CREATION
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
My Creation helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MY CREATION
Study My Creation like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Name family members in the nuclear and extended 

What this means
In this part you learn to name family members in the nuclear and extended . You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: name family members in the nuclear and extended .
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “My Creation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can name family members in the nuclear and extended . Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what My Creation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “My Creation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: name family members in the nuclear and extended )

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach My Creation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: name family members in the nuclear and extended .
3. Make one local Kenya example of My Creation from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for My Creation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study My Creation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is a family the family tree?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what My Creation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: name family members in the nuclear and extended .

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
